draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Mandrem! At high tide the sea rushes into Mandrem Creek, which runs right alongside the beach. This quiet white-sand stretch between Morjim and Arambol is also a notified turtle nesting site.
draft.hungryLine: Mandrem's beach shacks do fresh fish, and a few cafes in Junas Waddo are worth the walk.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Bhumika Devi Temple is a 2 minute walk, Holy Cross Chapel about 7, and Our Lady of the Rosary Church about 16.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Laze on the beach and watch local fishermen haul in their catch.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The village was first called Manjrey. The Portuguese turned it into Mandrem, because in Portuguese the D was said like a J.

tips.title: Catch the high tide.
tips.body: Mandrem looks its best at high tide, when seawater floods into the creek beside the beach.

tips.title: Swim with care.
tips.body: The water off Mandrem gets surprisingly deep.

story.title: Manjrey
story.body: The village was originally called Manjrey. It had a small fishing community that still works the beach today.

story.title: A new name and a fort
story.body: The Portuguese renamed it Mandrem and left a small fort nearby. The fort is now a high-class hotel with views to Maharashtra.

story.title: Turtles protected
story.body: Mandrem Beach was notified as a turtle nesting site under the 2011 coastal rules.

story.title: Quiet by choice
story.body: With Junas and Ashvem beaches and 11 wards, Mandrem is a calm spot 21 km from Panaji.

food.detail: Beach shack for fish, and eating here gets you a lounger for the day
